doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Nicki Parrott and acoustic versus electric bass
summary: Pallo found Nicki Parrott for the Iridium group and prefers acoustic bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: You’ve got a nice little group there too at the Iridium with —

Nicki Parrott’s on bass, correct. And she is fabulous. We found her, well I saw her first and told Les, I said, “Les, I heard this female bass player.” He says “aww, she can’t play bass.” I says, “Les, you have to hear her.” So she came in and sat in with us on a couple of songs and he said whoa, he couldn’t believe it. Because he figured it’s a girl—
Because of her smaller hands and so forth, but she plays that acoustic bass. She’s great. And then we hired her. She’s been with us now like, I’m not too sure, five years maybe.
Do you notice, is there any discernable difference in playing with an acoustic as opposed to an electric bass?
What is the difference for you?

For me I prefer the acoustic. And you could have it amplified of course but the acoustic of the bass still comes out. It has more bottom and warmer I would say. If you do play the electric bass you really have to get someone that really is playing the correct notes. Because now the notes are really going to be heard and popped out.

They better play the right notes. And the right patterns. If you’re going to walk with the bass and so forth. I think you can probably get away with it on an acoustic a little bit, but I’d rather work with the acoustic. It gives you a little more bottom.
